Hard to find, easy to regret
Apr 2026 • Friends
Recommended by our guide, we had a reservation at 8.30pm but had trouble finding the property. No visible “Cau Go” sign — only “Fu Rong Hua” on the façade, which is misleading (we had passed by).
We even received a message that our reservation could not be maintained. On arrival, the welcome was rather cold.
We ordered a dish that we were initially advised against because it supposedly required an hour of preparation — it finally arrived in just 30 minutes. We were then told that this would be the last dish we could order, as the kitchen closed.
If the location is excellent, the service has been quite indifferent and not customer oriented. Prices are also significantly higher than local restaurants, making the experience even more disappointing.
In summary: ideal location, but confusing access, poor service and insufficient price/quality ratio.

The worst meal we've had in a very long time
Mar 2026 • Family
We came to Cau Go expecting a great traditional Vietnamese meal only to be thoroughly disappointed. With so many decent restaurants in Hanoi I don't understand how they remain in business. The card our menus were printed on were envious of the dry, rigid chicken we ate. The batter on the soft shell crab was inches thick and even the fresh spring rolls were tough to eat. I cannot remember the last time we ate a meal this ordinary or left food on the table. The room was exceptionally noisy. Needless to say we won't go back. The service staff were friendly and efficient however.

Not special
Dec 2025 • Couples
This restaurant did not live up to expectations.

We visited this restaurant on the last night of a month long trip all over Vietnam. On the night we visited only the 6th floor was open so we were not able to enjoy the terrace on the 7th floor. It was not clear why.

Tables for 2 were very close together so lacked privacy.

The food is really not special. We have eaten much better food in many places all over Vietnam.

The restaurant is grubby. The glass doors overlooking the lake were dirty.

The restaurant opened for evening service at 5.30. We arrived at 6pm. I used restroom to wash my hands. The bin in the toilet was already overflowing with toilet paper. My wife used the ladies which she said was grubby and smelled of tobacco smoke. 

This place is a tourist trap and not special. We are mystified as to what the Michelin 2025 recognition was for.

A complete letdown at Cao Go
Nov 2025 • Couples
I normally don’t write reviews, but my recent dinner at Cau Go in Hanoi was disappointing enough that I feel the need to share my experience. My wife and I went there based on recommendations from the internet and from our hotel, hoping to enjoy traditional Vietnamese cuisine. Unfortunately, the evening turned out to be quite unpleasant.

To begin with, when we asked for the restroom, we were told it was four floors below in a different restaurant. The facilities were in poor condition, and there was nothing to dry my hands with. When I asked for help, they handed me a single tissue, which felt far from hygienic.

The atmosphere wasn’t any better: the place was very noisy, the décor felt cheap, and the food itself was underwhelming. The beef we ordered was rubbery, the black chicken completely lacked seasoning, and the wine glasses were so small that they held barely two sips. As if that wasn’t enough, a rat ran underneath our table from one side to the other just as we were finishing our meal.

When it came time to pay, our server, Kitty, became unusually pushy about us leaving a positive review on Google. After I told her I would do it later, she went to my wife and insisted again—so persistently that we had to pretend we didn’t have internet access just to end the conversation.

I’m seriously surprised that this place is recommended as “high-end Vietnamese cuisine.” It was honestly the worst restaurant experience I’ve ever had, and I wouldn’t wish it on anyone.
